uncertain.note: page quality: this is a clean CUDL colour scan of the leaf, far better than the Gallica film used for p041. Ink is even, the paper shows scattered brown fibres and a few show-through marks from the verso, and nothing on the page is damaged or lost. Readings below are doubts about the setting, not about legibility.

set in spaced capitals (P A R L E M E N T  D E  T H O L O S E .) and closed up per §3. It ends with a point, not the comma p041 prints. The schema has no spaced_caps field for running_head, so the letterspacing is recorded here.

uncertain.note: 'coupees' is printed with NO acute. At 3x the slanted brown mark above the first e is a paper fibre (brown, not black, and it runs on past the letter), unlike the true black acutes of 'cachée' (lines[6]) and 'donné' (lines[9]) on the same page. Reader B may read 'coupées'.

uncertain.note: a faint horizontal mark sits over the e of 'de'; at 3x it is show-through from the verso, not a macron ('dẽ' is not a word and the mark has none of the weight of the real tildes on this page, 'cõtinence', 'tellemẽt', 'd'hõme').

uncertain.text: ou fait le malefice.) quelquesfois enuers vne ſeule:
uncertain.note: the print sets a space between the point and the closing parenthesis ('malefice . )'). Closed up here per §1 (parentheses: space outside, none inside). The mark after 'ſeule' is a colon, two dots, checked at 5x.

uncertain.text: Gaſcongne) par celuy qui la fait & ordonné {d}. car com-
uncertain.note: small capitals: the initial G is a small-capital G — cap form, but only x-height (compare the full-height P of 'Philoſophes' on the next line and the lowercase double-storey g of '-congne' in the same word). Transcribed as an ordinary capital per §3. Reader B may read a lowercase 'gaſcongne'. The print sets 'gaſcongne)par' with no space after the parenthesis; normalized per §1.

uncertain.text: ſe qui ſe peut lier, ſe peur deſlier, & diſſouldre {e}. Dont
uncertain.note: sic: 'ſe peur deſlier' where the sense wants 'ſe peut deſlier' (the same phrase is set correctly as 'ſe peut lier' earlier in the line). At 5x the final letter is an unmistakable r with its shoulder arm, not a t; no crossbar. Transcribed as printed. 'deſlier' is ſ+l (the second stroke is a plain l with no ſ nub), not ſſ; 'diſſouldre' is a true ſſ ligature.

uncertain.text: ne ſuffit point pour deffaire le mariage ja contracté {f}.
uncertain.note: 'ja' is printed with a j: at 5x the letter carries a dot above and a descender hooked left below the baseline, unlike the plain i of 'iour' on the next line (checked side by side). Kept as printed per §2 (i/j as printed); reader B may normalize to 'ia'.

uncertain.text: ſe pour! diſſouldre le mariage: attendu que Dieu ne
uncertain.note: a sort of unclear identity stands between 'pour' and 'diſſouldre' where nothing belongs. At 12x (pages/strips/p043/body-6.jpg, second line, x about 220-250 of 1699) it is a heavy wedge tapering downwards from ascender height to just above the baseline, with a separate small dot below it — the shape of an exclamation mark, which is how it is transcribed. It could equally be a turned 'i' or a wrong sort pulled from another case; it is certainly not a marker (markers on this page are small italic letters, and z a b c d e f g h i k are all accounted for). A human should decide whether to keep '!' or record it as an unidentified sort.

uncertain.note: the print sets 'delaquelle' with hairline gaps of equal width between 'de', 'la' and 'quelle'. Read as 'de' + 'laquelle' (laquelle being a single word of the period, §1); reader B may read 'de la quelle'. 'a la femme' carries no grave, as printed.

uncertain.note: the line-end break sign after 'diſſo' prints as a short low stub, close to a point in shape, not as the full horizontal bar seen at 'demeu-' on lines[38]. spacing normalized throughout per §1: commas set tight ('croyable,ſi' lines[12], 'humains,toute' lines[18], 'chair,que,quand' lines[36], 'ans,comme' lines[39]), a colon set tight before & ('amortie:&' lines[38]), '&' set tight ('huit&' lines[39]), words set tight ('ont ainſi' lines[2], 'de laquelle' lines[32], 'lues de la chair' lines[36], 'mariage ja' lines[21]), and parentheses ('gaſcongne)par' lines[17], 'd'hõme)le' lines[33]). Nothing is added or removed beyond spacing.

two line breaks are printed with no word-break hyphen and are transcribed as printed: lines[4] 'ne peu' + lines[5] 'uent'; lines[18] 'toute cho' + lines[19] 'ſe'. Hyphens print normally elsewhere on the page, so these are compositor omissions (§1 says such a break needs no entry; recorded here only for the reconciler's convenience).

the tall letter of 'fin' is read as f, not long ſ: at 12x the stem carries a crossbar to the LEFT of the stem at x-height and the following i's dot is absorbed into the fi ligature, the same shape as the unambiguous 'fin' of note g ('Au c. fin &'). 'c. fin.' = capitulo finali, as p041 prints 'c. final.'.
at 8x there is a point after the q and after the v, giving 'xxvj. q. v. c. ſi'; the points are small and sit low. Reader B may read 'xxvj. q v. c. ſi'.

the canon meant is 'Si per sortiarias' (as note g spells it, 'c ſi per ſortia|rias'), but here at 14x only one narrow round letter stands between 'ſo' and 'iarias' — a clear open c, with no room for the 'rt' pair. Transcribed as printed, 'ſociarias'. The mark over the o is the long ſ's top flag, not a macron.

sic: 'fina' where 'final.' is expected (cf. notes d and f, 'final. de frig.'). At 12x the fi ligature is clear, then n, then an unmistakable round a with its tail; there is no l, no point and no tilde. Reader B may read 'c. final & il'.

sic: the note ends on 'ma' with no point and nothing following on the line (checked to the right edge of the margin column); the expected 'malef.' or 'mal.' is not completed, and note d begins on the next line. Cf. notes d and f, which both close properly with '& mal.'.
the line ends with a lone c followed by a clear short hyphen, continued by 'final.' on the next line ('au c-|final' = au chapitre final). Transcribed as printed.
no point is printed after the leading 'c' (the space between c and ſi is empty at 8x); elsewhere the same formula is set 'c.'. Transcribed as printed.

the key letter of this note is set as a ROMAN CAPITAL K, not the italic lowercase k of the body marker; the rest of the note is in the ordinary margin italic. Keyed 'k' per the printer's alphabet (…h i k…) and the body marker on blocks[0].lines[33]. Line 2 'tem. P. xxvij' carries no final point.

placement: the margin column is full (42 printed note lines against 40 body lines), so the notes do not sit level with their markers. Measured against the body lines, note z begins beside blocks[0].lines[2] though its marker is on lines[4]; a beside lines[3] (marker lines[5]); b beside lines[6] (marker lines[7]); c beside lines[10] (marker lines[11]); d beside lines[12], five lines above its marker on lines[17]; e beside lines[16] (marker lines[19]); f, g, h and k then fall level with their markers and i one line below. Every beside_line above is the nearest body line by vertical centre and is approximate to about half a line.

no signature, no catchword and no foot citation block. foot.jpg shows the leaf blank from just below the last body line to the trimmed edge; nothing is lost to the crop. The margin column also ends well above the foot (last note line 'q. ij.' stands beside body line 36).

the line-end sign after 'il' is a small raised stroke, transcribed '-' (the word runs on as 'il|lud'). The leading 'P.' throughout this page's margin is the paragraph mark used for Digest/Novels paragraphs, as on p041 ('P. per occaſio', 'P. j de nup.'); transcribed as the letter P per that precedent.

the word after 'ſi' ends in a round a with a point following ('ſerua.'); a terminal us-sign ('ſeruꝰ') cannot be wholly excluded at this size, but the glyph has the plain two-stroke italic a of 'adop.' on the line above.
